Schema 1.2.0 went live, the ingest pipeline learned to read the .xlsx workbook directly, the log was brought up to 18 August (270.17 h owed), an audit document for Vince and payroll was written and compiled, and a full-system review re-derived every published figure by an independent implementation — agreeing 92/92. decision.what: ingest.sh takes the whole .xlsx workbook, converted by scripts/xlsx_to_csv.py into the two CSVs the engine already accepts. Everything downstream is unchanged and the engine stays locked.
decision.why: The spreadsheet exports one tab per CSV but downloads whole, so the workbook is the only way to get hours and payments in one action. It also deleted the project's last quiet failure: a payments export in ~/downloads used to be silently ignored while nhs-log-ingest reported success.

decision.what: The converter zero-pads the Start hour (08:45). The canonical CSV was internally inconsistent — 32 of 47 rows padded, 15 not — so no rule reproduces it byte for byte.
decision.why: Proven the engine computes every day identically either way, so it is cosmetic. Padding matches the larger group, making the one-time reformat 12 rows instead of 32, and the converter is the only writer from now on.

decision.what: The six rendered-page scenario files are committed under website/scripts/scenarios/ rather than generated at run time.
decision.why: A generated partial-payment scenario would pay the same 5400 min against a growing accrued total, so its expected figures would drift and the failure would read as engine drift. Committed files also keep the check independent of Python and the engine, and age loudly.

decision.what: A read-only daily staleness reminder (scripts/check-staleness.sh plus a systemd user timer at 11:00, Persistent=true), instead of update.sh.
decision.why: A timer cannot fetch the workbook or publish, so the only step left to automate was already one command. The real failure mode is forgetting — the git history shows an irregular 2–3 week cadence. And a timer that ran the ingest would dirty the working tree on every run.

decision.what: The audit document identifies the author fully (name, position, NHS email) and lives in gitignored tmp/, uncommitted, source and PDF.
decision.why: Reverses an earlier "in the repo, identity-light" choice. The repo is public, so the way to have a fully identified internal NHS document is to keep it out of the repo rather than strip the identity out of it.

decision.what: The review's centrepiece was a fresh reimplementation of the counting rules that never imports afc_hours and classifies every worked minute individually — a different algorithm from the engine's segment-splitting.
decision.why: Re-running the engine's own tests proves nothing a shared bug would not also pass. Two implementations agreeing across 58 days is evidence; one agreeing with itself is none.

warnings.warning: THE `!` PREFIX AND THE BASH TOOL RUN IN A CONTAINER whose HOME is /home/filipejunqueira/containers/claude-home, NOT /home/filipejunqueira. Anything writing to the user's real ~ (systemd units, dotfiles, ~/.local/bin) must be given to the user to run in their own terminal. A `systemctl --user link` run with `!` reported "Created symlink" and put it where the real user systemd never looks.

`systemctl --user enable` on an ABSOLUTE PATH symlinks only the file named — a timer enabled that way fails with "Refusing to start, unit X.service to trigger not loaded" because its service was never linked. Link both. And keep each command on ONE line: a wrapped line gave "Too few arguments" and then tried to execute the unit file.
`rm -rf` is denied by the user's global settings with no exceptions. Build a fresh directory rather than clearing one; `rm -f` on single files is fine.

The Bash tool's working directory PERSISTS between calls in this environment (contrary to the older snapshot's claim). A `cd website` in one call leaves the next call there — this caused three failed commands this session. Use absolute paths or cd explicitly every time.
`cp` is aliased to `cp -i` (use `command cp -f`) and `ls` to lsd (use `command ls` for flags like -la --time-style).
Running regen.sh or ingest.sh to "check" something rewrites generated_at in BOTH committed copies of web_data.json. Build payloads in memory instead; the review did this throughout.

tmp/ holds internal NHS documents (the BHLY database write-up and X-drive triage) kept as formatting references, plus the uncommitted audit document. It is gitignored as of 2026-08-18 — do not un-ignore it, and never commit its contents to this PUBLIC repo.

The global ruff hook reformats any .py on write and removes imports added in an earlier tool call than their first usage. The shellcheck hook blocks a .sh write on any finding — a rejected write is the hook working.

`[[ cond ]] && cmd` as a standalone statement under `set -e` exits the script when the condition is false. This was a real bug in ingest.sh, caught by review; it is written as full `if` statements now with the reason in a comment.
